title: Scratch declaration for the ordinary-day P(spread > +5 bp) of H5's spread models against persistence-logistic (#844)
status: exploration on development data; nothing here is a verdict under scoring protocol v1 (#640). Declared by the pull request that closes #844 before any number was computed. No variant is added to a published declaration, no rule changes, and the live record and pin do not move.
hypothesis: H5 (primary goal), step 3 (evaluation): the 'no ordinary-day ranking gain' half of H5's kill rule, for the current spread models. Avenue #807.

span.note: A target day after 2025-12-31 is refused (LookAheadError) and so is a locked day (docs/decisions/lockbox.md). The directive (#844 criterion 4) fixes this end; the 2026 development days that metadata/exploration_684.json admits for other re-runs are not read here. The third regime, labelled 2025-26 by repo_model.reliability_regimes.REGIMES, therefore holds the days of 2025 only.

event: the target day's spread_bps exceeds +5 bp as repo_model.data.exceeds_bp reads it (the whole-basis-point event)
unit: one cell is a target day at one lead h = 1..5. Each row's forecast of target day s at lead h is the probability made h business days earlier (the decision day), exactly as the walk of its own script made it.

spread_mr_level10.label: mean reversion (#686)
spread_mr_level10.source: repo_model.spread_mean_reversion.walk on the published panel, via scripts/spread_mean_reversion_686.py build_frame; P(> 5 bp) is repo_model.spread_mean_reversion.exceedance of the lead's 23 quantiles

spread_mr_ctx.label: (i) context-pooled residuals (#761)
spread_mr_ctx.source: repo_model.spread_mr_variants.walk via scripts/spread_mr_variants_761.py build_frame; the same reading of the 23 quantiles

c_two_part_new.label: (c) two-part, #634
c_two_part_new.source: the walk of scripts/spread_distribution_634.py walk --variant c_two_part_new on the scratch panel built by the commands in that script's docstring; P(> 5 bp) is that script's exceedance() of the 23 quantiles

gbm_funding.label: gbm_funding, #634
gbm_funding.source: the walk of scripts/spread_distribution_634.py walk --variant gbm_funding; the same reading

persistence_logistic.label: the project's persistence-logistic
persistence_logistic.source: repo_model.baseline.persistence_logistic_exceedance through rolling_exceedance_backtest, as scripts/spread_distribution_634.py exceedance builds it at tau = 5 bp, one walk per lead; the project's own, not an approximation. The paired comparisons are against it.

as_of_spread.label: the raw as-of spread
as_of_spread.source: spread_bps of the anchor row of the decision day (protocol_benchmarks._anchor: the last row public at the decision instant). It is a score, not a probability: only its AUROC is reported, and its pairing with persistence-logistic is on AUROC alone.

ordinary_days.definition: the target day is not a risk date under repo_model.risk_dates.NON_ORDINARY, read with reporting_on = the target day (the reading of H5's context rule and of the pressure-day type of #632's page)
ordinary_days.sensitivity: repo_model.risk_dates.SCHEDULED, the judge's risk_date grouping, on the same cells. Which definition H2 and H5 read is Eleonora's open ruling (#800); both are shown and neither is preferred.

days: per lead, the target days on which every row, persistence-logistic and the raw as-of spread have a value, with the target on or before 2025-12-31

splits.pooled: shown beside the regimes, never alone (#670)

metrics.auroc: the probability that a pressure day outranks an ordinary non-pressure day, ties counted half
metrics.brier: mean squared error of the probability
metrics.reliability: the slope and intercept of logit P(y = 1) = intercept + slope * logit(p), fitted by repo_model.reliability_regimes.fit (#683's helper, unchanged); 1 and 0 for a reliable forecast

interval.kind: stationary bootstrap of the cell's days in date order
interval.seed: 844 * 1000 + 100 * lead + 10 * regime index (pooled 0, then the regimes in order) + 5 * (1 if the SCHEDULED sensitivity else 0)
interval.paired: each resample draws one index set and scores every row on it, so a difference from persistence-logistic (row minus persistence-logistic, for AUROC, Brier, slope and intercept) is paired. Positive AUROC difference and negative Brier difference favour the row.
interval.undefined: a resample on which a metric is undefined (it drew no pressure day, or the fit has no maximum) is counted; a metric undefined on more than 5% of its resamples reports no interval

minimum_pressure_days.rule: Eleonora's #710 minimum: a cell with fewer than 3 pressure days reports no AUROC, slope or intercept (event-based metrics); its Brier and counts are shown. A slope without an interval where the cell has fewer than 5 pressure days, as repo_model.reliability_regimes does.

counts: every cell reports its days and its pressure days
closing_lines: the page ends with one line per row against H5's ordinary-day kill clause ('no ordinary-day ranking gain'), labelled development. A line only counts the regime-by-lead cells with at least 3 pressure days in which the row's paired AUROC difference from persistence-logistic has an interval above zero, covering zero, or below zero. It sets no threshold and gives no verdict: what counts as a gain is Eleonora's.
not_done: no variant is added; no new fit is made beyond the walks of the scripts named above
no day after 2025-12-31 is read; no locked day is scored
no judge, registration or published figure is changed
